note: F-167: the contract used to assert only tautologies (`x >= 0 || x < 0`, `assert(true)`), so no input could make it fail and the golden pinned bytes that constrained nothing. The caller now supplies the expected shift / AND / OR / XOR results and the contract checks them; `~` is checked by double inversion and De Morgan's law, which hold under OP_INVERT's byte semantics as well as integer semantics (OP_INVERT on 12 leaves 0xf3 = -115 on chain, not -13). Every expected value below is worked out by hand from the source with a = 12 (0x0c), b = 10 (0x0a) — one-byte operands whose results stay minimal and below 0x80 — not taken from compiler output. No signature is involved; this spec runs the fixture's compiled bytes through @bsv/sdk's consensus Spend.validate() for an accept AND a wrong-value near-miss reject.

spends.note: near-miss: wrong precomputed left-shift result (49 != 48) — OP_NUMEQUALVERIFY fails
near-miss: wrong precomputed right-shift result (7 != 6) — the final OP_NUMEQUAL leaves false
near-miss: 24 is 12 << 1, what a shift lowering that dropped or mis-pushed the count would produce
near-miss: AND and OR results swapped — what an OP_AND/OP_OR mix-up would produce
